records.name: Hazel J. Doyle
records.bio: Doyle co-authored both the University College Dublin collection reconstruction and the later survey of Blaschka models across Irish institutions. The studies combine archival order evidence with later museum registers, condition data and collection movements.

records.name: Federigo Federighi
records.bio: Federighi’s openly licensed photograph documents a group of Blaschka cnidarian models at the Natural History Museum of Pisa University. The project includes him as a modern documentation actor because the image provides a verifiable public visual anchor for the collection.

records.name: Holly Daws
records.bio: Daws is named in National Museums Scotland’s conservation account of a damaged Blaschka model. The treatment record makes her part of the objects’ later material biography, documenting cleaning, stabilization, support making, colour matching and rebonding.

records.name: C. Giles Miller
records.roles: museum scientist · Natural History Museum collection historian
records.bio: Miller co-authored the principal published inventory and collection history of the Natural History Museum’s Blaschka holdings. The study is a central reference for acquisition, survival and object-level reconstruction in the London collection.

records.name: Miranda Lowe
records.roles: museum scientist · collection historian · object authentication
records.bio: Lowe co-authored the Natural History Museum collection history and later appears in technical authentication work on original Blaschka components. Her record therefore joins published collection reconstruction to object-level museum expertise.

records.name: Eva Rydlová
records.bio: Rydlová co-authored the conservation and technical study of the National Museum in Prague’s surviving Blaschka octopus. The work documents damage, construction and treatment while anchoring one of the best-studied individual zoological models.

records.name: Ivana Kopecká
records.bio: Kopecká co-authored the conservation and technical study of the National Museum in Prague’s surviving Blaschka octopus. Her work contributes directly to the object’s documented construction, damage and restoration history.

records.name: John Armitage
records.bio: Armitage salvaged and carried out some restoration on the Leeds Blaschka sea-anemone models in 1959. The surviving account does not support a treatment count or object-by-object reconstruction, but it establishes a named intervention in the collection’s post-war survival history.
records.open: The number of models treated, techniques used and individual object assignments remain undocumented.

records.name: Katherine Larson
records.bio: Larson’s Corning-based research assembled a global picture of surviving Blaschka collections and historical distribution. Her 2016 account is an important modern census point for the project’s own collection-mapping work.

records.name: Helena Wouters
records.bio: Wouters is named among the IRPA analysts who examined glass, adhesives and paint layers in the Liège Blaschka collection. Her work belongs to the analytical strand of the collection’s restoration and redisplay project.
